item.title: Loyalist ends private placement, closes shares-for-debt deal
item.description: The CSE-listed explorer said no further tranches of its placement will close, while it settled $113,285 of debt through a separate share issuance.
item.content:encoded: Loyalist Exploration Limited (CSE: PNGC) said it has terminated its previously announced non-brokered private placement, originally announced on August 10, 2026, and that no further tranches or closings will be completed. The company said the first tranche of that offering, consisting of 25,000,000 common shares at $0.04 each for gross proceeds of $1,000,000 and closed on August 31, 2026, represents the offering's final closing. Haywood Securities Inc. acted as finder, receiving $37,200 in cash and 930,000 warrants at $0.075 until August 2028. Separately, Loyalist closed a shares-for-debt transaction, settling an aggregate of $113,285 of outstanding indebtedness owed to certain creditors through the issuance of 2,832,125 common shares, also priced at $0.04 each. Of that total, $45,000 owed to president and chief executive Errol Farr and vice-president of exploration Leonard Mackenzie was settled through the issuance of 1,125,000 shares combined. All shares issued in the transaction carry a hold period of four months and one day. Loyalist said it is relying on exemptions from the formal valuation and minority approval requirements in sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 for the related-party portion of the debt settlement, on the basis that neither component of the transaction exceeded 25% of the company's market capitalization. Separately, it said proceeds of the placement's first tranche are funding ongoing National Instrument 43-101 technical work on its Tully project, including a resource estimate and a preliminary economic assessment, as well as continuing production permitting work.

item.title: Lexaria reports animal-study results for CBD formulation
item.description: The company says one new DehydraTECH-CBD formulation produced a 566% improvement in brain absorption in an animal study, and has filed three related patent applications.
item.content:encoded: Lexaria Bioscience Corp. (NASDAQ:LEXX), which describes itself as a global innovator in drug-delivery platforms, said on October 15, 2026 that it has results from an animal study designated GLP-1-A26-1. The study evaluated formulation enhancements using both DehydraTECH-CBD compositions and DehydraTECH-semaglutide glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) compositions, with the stated aims of exploring potential for additional improved performance and staking new intellectual property claims. The release's single headlined figure concerns one CBD formulation, designated ALT2: in brain tissue sampled eight hours after dosing, it produced a mean concentration of 62.8 ± 34.3 ng/g, compared with 9.42 ± 1.91 ng/g for the study's reference formulation. The company characterizes that difference as a 566% improvement in mean brain absorption of DehydraTECH-CBD. The study was conducted in Sprague-Dawley rats across eleven treatment arms, with pharmacokinetics measured in blood plasma and in brain tissue over a period the release describes as running from eight to twenty-four hours after dosing. Alongside the CBD arms, the study tested DehydraTECH-semaglutide formulations of the GLP-1 compound semaglutide, which the release describes as pursuing the same two goals: additional improved performance and new intellectual property claims. Lexaria said it has already filed three new patent applications related to the formulations evaluated in the study, to protect this new intellectual property. The release states plainly that because these patent applications are not yet published, the company will not be providing full details of all the specific formulations evaluated — a limit the company places on its own disclosure, stated in those terms in the release. Chief executive Rich Christopher was quoted in the release: 'We are delighted that certain new formulations in this Study achieved our highest-ever DehydraTECH pharmaceutical-grade relative absorption performance.' The quote is general to the study's formulations as a group, and the release does not tie it to any single figure or treatment arm among those described above, including the 566% brain-absorption result. The release was issued from Kelowna, British Columbia — Lexaria's home base — under an October 15, 2026 dateline, and distributed through TheNewswire. It closes with Lexaria's standard forward-looking-statement disclaimer, cautioning that factors including regulatory uncertainty and competitive pressure could cause actual results to differ from any expectations suggested by the study, a caution that applies to every figure reported above.

item.title: Robo.ai shareholders to vote on 1-for-25 reverse split
item.description: The Nasdaq-listed, Dubai-based company set an October 26 meeting on the share consolidation, record date October 14, effective date November 6 if approved.
item.content:encoded: Robo.ai Inc. (Nasdaq: AIIO), a UAE-based, U.S.-listed company, has called an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for October 26, 2026, to approve a 1-for-25 reverse stock split of all classes of its ordinary shares. The meeting is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Dubai time) at the Meydan Grandstand, sixth floor, in Dubai, with a record date of October 14, 2026. If shareholders approve it, the split will take effect November 6, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET, consolidating every 25 existing shares into one. The company's 13,817,501 Class A ordinary shares would become 552,701 Class A shares, and its 222,116,290 Class B ordinary shares would become 8,884,684 Class B shares. The post-split shares will trade under a new CUSIP, G6693P130, the company said. A reverse stock split reduces the number of shares outstanding by combining multiple shares into one, without changing a shareholder's proportional stake in the company other than for fractional adjustments. Robo.ai said no fractional shares will be issued under the proposed 1-for-25 split: a shareholder otherwise entitled to a fraction of a share will instead receive a full share. Robo.ai said it expects the Class B trading price to increase proportionately once the split takes effect, though it gave no assurance the post-split price would reach twenty-five times its level beforehand; the post-split shares will trade under a new CUSIP, G6693P130. The October 26 meeting will also consider increasing authorized share capital by up to 25 million new Class A ordinary shares and 280 million new Class B ordinary shares, and adopting a seventh amended and restated memorandum and articles of association. Robo.ai is headquartered in Dubai and lists its Class B ordinary shares on Nasdaq under the ticker AIIO. The release sets out the mechanics of the proposed split and the meeting but does not state a reason for the consolidation; completion depends on shareholder approval, and if approved, the company said the split becomes effective November 6, 2026.

item.title: NXG Cushing Midstream Energy Fund to rename, broaden mandate
item.description: The fund's Board of Trustees approved renaming it and broadening its investment policy from midstream energy to energy infrastructure, effective December 18.
item.content:encoded: The NXG Cushing® Midstream Energy Fund (NYSE: SRV), a closed-end fund, said its Board of Trustees has approved changing the fund's name to The NXG Cushing® Energy Infrastructure Fund, effective December 18, 2026. The fund's ticker symbol, SRV, and its CUSIP, 231631300, will remain unchanged, according to the announcement, which was released October 16, 2026, from the fund's Dallas offices. Alongside the name change, the Board approved amending the fund's non-fundamental investment policies. The fund's rule requiring at least 80% of its assets to be invested in a defined category will shift that category from "midstream energy investments" to "energy infrastructure investments." The release states that as of October 15, 2026, approximately 90% of the Fund's net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, already consisted of energy infrastructure investments, and that the Fund therefore does not anticipate any change to its investment approach or rebalancing of its portfolio as a result of the amendment. No shareholder approval or action is required for either the name change or the policy amendment, the release said. No shareholder vote or other approval was required for either change, the release said, and investors need take no action; the fund's New York Stock Exchange listing and CUSIP are unaffected. Beyond the name, the policy amendment and the asset figures above, the release discloses no further detail about the Board's reasoning.

item.title: Emergent Metals restates Q2 financials, updates Lahontan deal
item.description: The TSX Venture-listed explorer corrected prior filings and said shareholders will vote on its acquisition by Lahontan Gold on December 4.
item.content:encoded: Emergent Metals Corp. (TSXV: EMR, OTCQB: EGMCF, FRA: EML) has filed amended and restated unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, replacing the statements and management's discussion and analysis it originally filed on August 28, 2026. The company said the amended filings "correct certain accounting and disclosure matters identified following the filing of the Original Filings," without specifying what those matters were. The restatement reduced share capital and accumulated other comprehensive loss by US$231,040. It increased comprehensive loss by US$263,894 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and by US$297,428 for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Emergent said the corrections had no effect on the company's assets, liabilities, net loss, total equity or cash balance. Separately, Emergent provided an update on its proposed acquisition by Lahontan Gold Corp. under an arrangement agreement dated September 15, 2026. Under a plan of arrangement, a court-supervised process used in Canada to combine companies, Lahontan would acquire all of Emergent's issued and outstanding common shares in exchange for 0.3115 of a Lahontan share for each Emergent share held — equivalent to about one Lahontan share for every 3.21 Emergent shares. The TSX Venture Exchange has given conditional acceptance to the transaction. Emergent said its shareholders are scheduled to vote on the arrangement at a meeting set for December 4, 2026, and that completion remains subject to shareholder approval, court approval, final TSXV acceptance and other required approvals. The release pointed to further transaction details in Emergent's September 16, 2026 news release and to the arrangement agreement itself, filed on SEDAR+. The company also reminded holders of common share purchase warrants issued in private placements completed on November 14 and 19, 2024 that those warrants are scheduled to expire on November 14 and 19, 2026, respectively, at an exercise price of C$0.10. The release described the warrants as non-transferable and said no extension is currently intended. The release does not state a termination fee, identify a special committee, or say whether the transaction was negotiated at arm's length. It noted that the arrangement agreement and plan of arrangement are available under Emergent's and Lahontan's respective profiles on SEDAR+.

item.title: Azitra to execute 1-for-10 reverse stock split
item.description: The NYSE American-listed dermatology biopharmaceutical company's shares begin trading on a split-adjusted basis October 26, 2026.
item.content:encoded: Azitra, Inc. (NYSE American: AZTR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for precision dermatology, said its board of directors has approved a 1-for-10 reverse stock split of its common stock. The split takes effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern time on October 26, 2026, and the company's shares will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis under a new CUSIP number, 05479L401, when the market opens that day. A reverse stock split combines multiple existing shares into a single new share, reducing the number outstanding without changing a holder's proportional ownership, apart from the effect of any fractional-share cash-out. Azitra's stockholders authorized the board, at the company's June 15, 2026 annual meeting, to select a ratio between 1-for-2 and 1-for-30; the board approved the final ratio of 1-for-10, together with the October 26 effective date, on October 14, 2026. The change will reduce outstanding shares from 60,603,742 to approximately 6,060,374. Azitra said stockholders holding shares through a brokerage account will have their holdings automatically adjusted to reflect the new ratio. Those entitled to a fractional share will instead receive cash, without interest, calculated from the average closing price of Azitra's common stock over the five trading days immediately preceding the effective date. The stock will continue to trade on NYSE American under the symbol AZTR, now under a new CUSIP, 05479L401, with Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Co. as transfer agent. Azitra describes itself as a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for precision dermatology. Its disclosed pipeline includes ATR-COSF, a recombinant protein candidate, and ATR-04, an investigational live biotherapeutic for EGFR inhibitor-associated rash, which the company said has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The release describes only the mechanics of the reverse split — the ratio, the effective date, the resulting share count and the fractional-share treatment. It does not state a business rationale for the chosen ratio or the timing of the change.

item.title: Canadian wholesale sales fell 1.6% in August
item.description: Statistics Canada said sales excluding petroleum and grain products dropped to $91.6 billion, even as sales ran 7.2% above a year earlier.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada reported that wholesale sales, excluding petroleum, petroleum products, other hydrocarbons, and oilseed and grain, fell 1.6% to $91.6 billion in August 2026. The agency said sales decreased in five of the sector's seven subsectors, together accounting for 70.6% of total wholesale sales. The largest decline came from the motor vehicle and motor vehicle parts and accessories subsector, which fell 3.8% to $15.1 billion. The agricultural supplies industry group posted the next-largest decrease, down 12.4% to $3.5 billion. The overall decline was moderated by the building material and supplies subsector, which rose 1.4% to $14.1 billion. Statistics Canada said wholesale sales were 7.2% higher in August than in the same month a year earlier. In volume terms — which adjust for price changes — wholesale sales, under the same exclusions, fell 1.8% in August. Wholesale inventories, excluding the same petroleum and grain-related categories, were unchanged in August at $141.0 billion. The inventory-to-sales ratio rose from 1.51 in July to 1.54 in August, a measure of how many months it would take to clear existing inventory at the current sales pace. Ontario posted the largest provincial decline, down 1.6% to $47.8 billion, following six months of consecutive increases, and Saskatchewan posted the second-largest decrease, down 8.2% to $3.8 billion. Statistics Canada also reported gains in several smaller jurisdictions: Prince Edward Island rose 5.1% to $125.1 million, Nova Scotia rose 0.6% to $1,400.1 million, and Alberta rose 0.7% to $10,378.9 million, while Nunavut rose 43.4% to $13.9 million. Statistics Canada said this release's content was produced with the assistance of a generative artificial intelligence tool and refined and verified by the agency's own experts.

item.title: Goldgroup completes C$101 million strategic investment in Luca Mining
item.description: Goldgroup Mining acquired subscription receipts expected to convert into roughly 19.9% of Luca Mining once its Cozamin Mine acquisition closes.
item.content:encoded: Goldgroup Mining Inc. (TSXV: GORO) (NYSE American: GORO) said it completed a C$101,123,662 strategic investment in Luca Mining Corp. on October 14, 2026, acquiring 101,123,662 subscription receipts at a price of C$1.00 per receipt. The receipts were issued as part of a bought-deal private placement that Luca is conducting in connection with its proposed acquisition of the Cozamin Mine, which the release refers to as the "Cozamin Acquisition" without further describing its terms. A subscription receipt is a security that converts into a common share once specified conditions are met, rather than granting share ownership immediately. Here, the receipts convert into Luca common shares once release conditions are satisfied, which the release says include completion of the Cozamin Acquisition. Goldgroup said it may elect to convert its receipts early, provided doing so would not take its holding above 19.9% of Luca's outstanding shares without further approval. Following conversion, Goldgroup said it will hold 101,123,662 Luca common shares, representing approximately 19.9% of Luca's outstanding shares on a non-diluted basis. The release does not state Luca's total share count on a diluted basis, nor does it give the total size of the bought-deal offering of which Goldgroup's receipts were a part. Goldgroup also secured an investor rights agreement with Luca. While Goldgroup holds at least 10% of Luca's shares, the agreement gives it the right to participate in future equity financings and top up its holding in relation to dilutive issuances, and the right to nominate two persons to Luca's board of directors. The release states that Goldgroup "intends to assess opportunities relating to its investment in Luca" and that, depending on its strategic priorities, market conditions and its evaluation of Luca's business, it may acquire additional securities, exercise its board nomination rights, or dispose of some or all of its position. The release does not name Luca's stock ticker or exchange, does not name any underwriter or agent for Luca's offering, and does not describe the terms of the Cozamin Mine acquisition — the price, the seller, or Luca's other obligations — beyond referring to it as a pending acquisition that conversion of the receipts is conditioned on. Goldgroup's contacts for the release are listed as Javier Reyes, chief executive officer, and Sophia Shane, in corporate development.

item.title: US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% over the year.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers rose 0.6 percent in September 2026 on a seasonally adjusted basis. Over the 12 months ending in September, the index rose 3.7 percent on a not-seasonally-adjusted basis, the bureau said. The index for all items less food and energy — commonly referred to as core CPI — rose 0.3 percent in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, and was up 2.6 percent over the year, not seasonally adjusted, according to the release. The bureau attributed much of the monthly increase to energy prices, stating that "the index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase." Over the 12-month period, it said "the energy index increased 20.4 percent... due in large part to the index for gasoline rising 34.2 percent." Shelter costs continued to rise: the bureau said "the shelter index rose 0.4 percent in September after rising 0.3 percent in August," with the shelter index up 3.2 percent over the year. The food index was unchanged in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, the bureau said, though it rose 2.5 percent over the preceding 12 months. The release reports the measured price changes for the month and the year; it includes no assessment of future price trends or monetary policy.

item.title: HawkEye 360 secures $36 million in new international contracts
item.description: The Q3 awards span more than 10 allied and partner nations across the Indo-Pacific, Middle East, Europe and the Americas, the company said.
item.content:encoded: HawkEye 360, Inc. (NYSE: HAWK) announced on October 15, 2026 that it secured $36 million in new international contracts during the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The release describes HawkEye 360 as "the global leader in signals intelligence data and analytics" and says the new awards reflect demand for its capabilities across more than 10 allied and partner nations. The release structures the new business as multi-year awards rather than one-time contracts, though it does not state the length of the multi-year terms or break the $36 million figure down by region, country or individual award. It groups the customers by region: the Indo-Pacific, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas. HawkEye 360 said these defense and intelligence customers are turning to its data and analytics "to strengthen situational awareness, identify emerging threats, and support timely operational decision-making" as they face what the company describes as increasingly complex security environments. The company's business, per its own description in the release, is built on detecting, geolocating and characterizing radio-frequency emissions worldwide from space-based collection, which it combines with proprietary signal processing and AI-powered analytics to produce what it calls domain awareness and early-warning indicators for the U.S. government and allied partners. Chief executive John Serafini said: "these awards reflect the growing recognition among allied nations that signals intelligence is essential to modern defense operations." He added that the company's focus remains on delivering capabilities that give "Warfighters and decision-makers" the information they need to understand the operational environment and act with confidence. The release names no specific country, government agency or company as a customer, and identifies no individual contract. It gives no revenue or backlog figures beyond the $36 million in new awards, and does not state a timetable for when the contracted work will be delivered or recognized as revenue.

item.title: Condor Energies sets October 15 closing for C$70-million financing
item.description: The combined public offering and private placement of 12% convertible debentures is expected to close with Research Capital and Canaccord Genuity as agents.
item.content:encoded: Condor Energies Inc. (TSX: CDR) (OTC: CNPRF) said it expects the closing of its previously announced financing to occur on October 15, 2026, or such other date as the company and its agents agree. The financing is intended to raise combined gross proceeds of up to C$70,000,000. It combines a public offering of up to C$25,000,000 and a concurrent non-brokered private placement of up to C$45,000,000, in each case consisting of 12% unsecured convertible debentures of the company priced at C$1,000 per debenture. Research Capital Corporation is acting as co-lead agent and sole bookrunner for the public offering, with Canaccord Genuity Corp. acting as co-lead agent. The public offering is being made under Condor's existing base shelf prospectus and a shelf prospectus supplement, both filed with securities regulators and accessible on SEDAR+. The release said the debentures are not being offered or sold in the United States or to U.S. persons and have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933. The release does not state how many debentures will be issued under either component of the financing, nor does it disclose a use of proceeds, a resale hold period, or any closing conditions beyond the expected date and the parties' ability to agree on a different one. Today's release updates the timing of a financing Condor had previously announced; it restates the price, size and parties involved but does not restate the full terms of that earlier announcement.

item.title: Prospect Ridge closes first tranche of flow-through placement
item.description: The CSE-listed explorer raised $1.35 million in its first tranche, with insiders buying in and proceeds earmarked for British Columbia exploration.
item.content:encoded: Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. (CSE: PRR) (OTC: PRRSF) (FRA: 0ED) said it has closed the first tranche of a non-brokered private placement of critical mineral flow-through units, first announced October 2, 2026. The first tranche issued an aggregate of 17,935,002 units priced at $0.075 each, for gross proceeds of $1,345,125.15. In connection with the first tranche, the company paid aggregate finder fees of $88,200.01 in cash and issued an aggregate of 1,176,000 finder warrants, each exercisable at $0.10 for two years, subject to acceleration on the occurrence of certain events the release did not specify. All securities issued in the first tranche, including the flow-through units, are subject to a statutory hold period expiring February 14, 2027. Insiders of the company purchased an aggregate of 335,000 of the units issued in the first tranche. The release describes this as the first tranche of the offering but does not state a target size for the placement overall, or when a further tranche might close. The company said the proceeds will go toward eligible Canadian exploration expenses on its British Columbia mineral projects, naming a focus on a 2,500-metre drill program at the Camelot project and preparations for spring drilling at the Excalibur project, north of Smithers. Prospect Ridge describes itself as a British Columbia-based exploration and development company focused on critical metals and gold, led by a management team it says has more than 100 years of combined mineral exploration experience, advancing projects in what it calls one of Canada's most under-explored mineral belts.

item.title: Scorpio Gold drills 36-metre gold intercept at Goldwedge
item.description: The Nevada driller's Phase Two program also returned high-grade hits at West Pit, Black Mammoth and the Zanzibar Trend, with a sonic program to follow.
item.content:encoded: Scorpio Gold Corp. (NASDAQ: SGLD) (TSXV: SGLD) (OTCQB: SRCRF) (FSE: RY9) on October 14, 2026 reported assay results from eight holes drilled as part of the Phase Two program at its wholly owned Manhattan District project in the Walker Lane Trend of Nevada. The lead result, hole 26MN-124 at the Goldwedge target, returned 2.94 g/t gold over 36.42 metres from a depth of 169.62 metres, including a higher-grade interval of 19.33 g/t gold over 4.27 metres from 188.36 metres, within faulted Zanzibar and Gold Hill formation rock. Hole 26MN-125 at West Pit returned 24.85 g/t gold over 1.22 metres from 150.88 metres within the Gold Hill Formation. Hole 26MN-121 at Black Mammoth returned 1.37 g/t gold over 17.07 metres from 275.54 metres within Zanzibar Formation mudstone, including a higher-grade 17.04 g/t gold over 1.07 metres at the brecciated contact between the Zanzibar mudstone and limestone units. Hole 26MN-122, along the Zanzibar Trend, returned 1.18 g/t gold over 17.10 metres from 47.21 metres, including 5.58 g/t gold over 2.59 metres, within brecciated metasediments of the Gold Hill Formation. The company said the results were verified by Leo Hathaway, P.Geo., its executive technical director, through review of laboratory certificates and field logs, inspection of blank, standard and duplicate sample performance, and chain-of-custody records. The release said assays have now been reported for 115 of the 122 holes drilled in the Phase Two program, totalling 33,379 of 35,844 metres, with results pending on the remaining seven holes. Manhattan carries a maiden inferred mineral resource estimate of 740,000 ounces of gold, from 18,343,000 tonnes grading 1.26 g/t gold, with an effective date of June 4, 2025 and a technical report dated October 23, 2025. The project includes the Goldwedge mine and four past-producing pits across a 4,780-hectare property in which Scorpio Gold holds a 100% interest. The company said it has scheduled a sonic drilling program, due to begin before the end of October 2026, to provide an initial test of the grade and tonnage of Manhattan's historic heap leach pad, tailings pond and low-grade stockpile. It also said it continues to evaluate underground mining potential at Goldwedge.

item.title: Eason Technology regains NYSE American listing compliance
item.description: A letter from NYSE Regulation resolves a listing-standards deficiency first flagged in October 2025, with another lapse now risking immediate delisting.
item.content:encoded: Eason Technology Limited (NYSE American: DXF) said it has received a letter from NYSE Regulation, dated October 8, 2026, confirming it has regained compliance with the exchange's continued listing standards. The letter resolves a deficiency under Section 1003(a)(ii) of the NYSE American Company Guide, which the exchange had first identified in letters to the company dated October 14, 2025 and December 30, 2025. The company said it demonstrated compliance with the applicable continued listing standards for two consecutive quarters, which it said satisfies the requirement under Section 1009(f) of the Company Guide for NYSE Regulation to confirm that a listed company has cured a deficiency. The release does not state which specific financial metric triggered the original deficiency notices, or describe the steps the company took over the past year to come back into compliance. Eason Technology describes its business as spanning real estate management, investment operations and digital technology security, with primary operations based in Hong Kong and China. The company said that under Section 1009(h) of the Company Guide, a further non-compliance finding within twelve months of the October 8 letter would lead NYSE Regulation to examine the relationship between the two incidents, and that depending on the circumstances the exchange may truncate its normal compliance procedures or begin delisting proceedings immediately rather than granting another cure period. Chief executive Stanley He said the company has achieved rapid growth across all of its business lines and that its corporate governance structure and financial position are at their strongest level since listing, adding that management places a high priority on compliant operations.

item.title: Getty Copper expands fall drill program past 20,000 metres
item.description: The expanded program follows spring results of 46 metres at 1.47% copper within a wider 150-metre interval at the Getty South target.
item.content:encoded: Getty Copper Inc. (TSXV: GTC, OTCQX: GTCDF) said on October 12 that it has expanded its fall drilling program at the Getty Project in British Columbia's Highland Valley Copper District to more than 20,000 metres, up from a previously planned 4,000 to 6,000 metres. Two drill rigs are currently operating at the Getty South target, the company said, with the expanded program also set to test other priority targets within the broader Getty Project area. The expansion follows results from the company's spring 2026 drilling campaign at Getty South, which returned 46 metres grading 1.47% copper within a broader 150-metre interval grading 0.71% copper. The release did not disclose the specific drill hole identifiers, assay methodology, or the full set of results from the spring program beyond this interval. Getty Copper holds an 82% interest in the Getty Property, located in British Columbia's Highland Valley Copper District and adjacent to Teck Resources' Highland Valley Copper mine, as well as a 100% interest in the neighbouring DOT Property. The company described the district as Canada's largest copper-producing area, though the release did not state current production figures for the district or for Teck's adjacent operation. Chief Executive Officer Ryan O'Regan was quoted: 'We look forward to finding more high grade copper mineralization at Getty South with this expanded program. Scaling up also gives us the bandwidth to begin to test our strong pipeline of newly defined exploration targets.' The release did not specify how many additional targets make up that pipeline or where they are located relative to Getty South. The company said the expanded program is intended to advance the Getty Project toward a mineral resource estimate in 2027. The release gave no further detail on the scope or timing of the studies that would be required to produce that estimate, nor on which zones beyond Getty South the resource would cover. Getty said the drilling is supported by a recently closed $15 million flow-through financing, which it said brought the company's cash position to approximately $20 million to accelerate exploration. The release did not state the financing's closing date, the number of units or shares issued, the subscription price, or the identity of any agent involved, nor whether the raise included warrants. Roy Greig, Ph.D., P.Geo., the company's Vice President of Exploration, reviewed and approved the scientific and technical information in the release as a qualified person under National Instrument 43-101. The release did not disclose a total budget for the expanded program or a timeline for reporting assay results from the new drilling.

item.title: Golden Shield signs binding LOI for C$6-million recapitalization
item.description: Walsh Karra Holdings would take an approximately 51% stake in the Guyana-focused gold company through subscription receipts priced at C$0.30.
item.content:encoded: Golden Shield Resources Inc. (CSE: GSRI) said it has signed a binding letter of intent with Walsh Karra Holdings for a strategic investment and recapitalization of up to C$6,000,000. Walsh Karra, through Aurevo Resources Inc., would invest C$5,000,000 directly, with up to a further C$1,000,000 available to existing shareholders and management, with both tranches priced at C$0.30 per subscription receipt. Each subscription receipt is structured to convert into one common share and one common share purchase warrant, with each warrant exercisable at C$0.39 for 24 months. Proceeds are to be held in escrow pending a list of conditions: renewal and issuance of Prospecting Licence PL 1/2021 at Golden Shield's 100%-owned, 5,457-hectare Marudi Mountain Project in Guyana's Rupununi Mining District, along with board approval, shareholder approval, and acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. If those conditions are not satisfied, the release said escrowed funds will be returned with interest. On closing, Walsh Karra would hold approximately 51% of Golden Shield on a fully diluted basis, which the release identified as a change of control. Leo Hathaway is stepping down from his combined Chairman and CEO role, with a new CEO to be appointed at closing; Hathaway and a person identified as Kalyan will be retained as Special Advisors for 12 months, and the board will be reconstituted to include investor nominees and an independent director. Marudi Mountain's Mazoa Hill deposit carries a 2017 historical estimate of 4.43 million tonnes grading 1.82 g/t gold (259,100 ounces) Indicated and 1.65 million tonnes grading 1.62 g/t gold (86,200 ounces) Inferred. The release stated that a qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify this historical estimate as current mineral resources or reserves, and that Golden Shield is not treating it as such. The company separately said it will acquire, in exchange for 13,000,000 common shares, a permanent worldwide licence to use, deploy, commercialize, sublicense and embed what it called the SimplyFI AI, traceable minerals and blockchain technology stack in connection with Marudi Mountain and its broader Guyana platform. The release gave no further description of the technology or its intended function beyond this licence grant. Golden Shield said there is a 90-day exclusivity period to negotiate a definitive agreement, and that the transaction is expected to close on or before January 6, 2027. The company said it may pay finder's fees of up to 5% of gross proceeds to eligible finders, and that all securities issued are subject to statutory hold periods and escrow requirements. The release did not name any agent or finder. Gregory R. Walsh, Walsh Karra's co-founder, was quoted describing Guyana as 'one of the most compelling mining jurisdictions in the hemisphere,' calling Marudi 'a standout asset.' Walsh Karra described itself in the release as a U.S.-based investment firm with a portfolio spanning artificial intelligence, data-centre infrastructure, climate ventures, and mining and natural resources.

item.title: Jaguar Uranium reports maiden resource at Laguna Salada
item.description: The estimate covers uranium and vanadium across about 4.3% of the land package at the company's project in Chubut Province, Argentina.
item.content:encoded: Jaguar Uranium Corp. (NYSE American: JAGU) said on October 13 that an independent Mineral Resource Estimate, compliant with SEC Regulation S-K 1300, has been completed for its Laguna Salada Uranium-Vanadium Project in Chubut Province, Argentina. The estimate, effective October 5, 2026, reports 4.2 million pounds of Indicated and 10.1 million pounds of Inferred U3O8 (uranium oxide), along with 31.1 million pounds of Indicated and 57.3 million pounds of Inferred V2O5 (vanadium pentoxide). In tonnage terms, the company reported 21.1 million tonnes in the Indicated category, grading 119 parts per million U3O8 equivalent, and 34.0 million tonnes Inferred, grading 170 ppm U3O8 equivalent. Jaguar said the mineralized footprint identified in the estimate covers approximately 4.3% of the 210,284-hectare Laguna Salada project area. The estimate was prepared by independent consulting firms Caracle Creek Chile SpA and Atticus Geoscience Consulting Ltd., who served as Qualified Persons on the disclosure. Chief Executive Officer Steven Gold was quoted saying the estimate 'marks a landmark milestone for Jaguar Uranium as we quantify the significant scale of Laguna Salada,' adding that it represents only about 4% of the total project area. The release's own headline characterized the estimate as highlighting 'significant potential for resource expansion' on that basis. Jaguar said its planned work program following the estimate includes approximately 250 new surface pits and trenches at the Pampa de Arroqui and Laguna Salada targets, 1,500 metres of sonic drilling at Buried Lake, and further metallurgical and field studies. The company reported a cash position of nearly US$18 million and no debt as of the announcement. The release did not disclose a timeline for the planned pitting, trenching or drilling program, nor any updated project economics, preliminary economic assessment, or capital cost estimate tied to the new resource. It also did not state what portion, if any, of the reported cash position is earmarked specifically for the program described.

item.title: IceCure presents 12-month breast cancer cryoablation data at EUSOBI
item.description: IceCure Medical reported 12-month data showing 97.5% objective response with cryoablation plus endocrine therapy and 91.7% with cryoablation alone, presented at a European breast imaging meeting.
item.content:encoded: IceCure Medical Ltd. (Nasdaq: ICCM), an Israel-based medical device company, said it presented 12-month clinical data on its ProSense cryoablation system for breast cancer treatment at the European Society of Breast Imaging's EUSOBI 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting in Maastricht, Netherlands. The company reported a 97.5% objective response rate among 40 patients treated with cryoablation in combination with endocrine therapy, and a 91.7% objective response rate among 24 patients treated with cryoablation alone. ProSense uses cryoablation, a technique that destroys tissue by freezing it, as an alternative to surgical removal of a tumor. The data IceCure presented covers a twelve-month follow-up period and compares outcomes between patients who received the device alongside endocrine therapy, a hormone-based treatment, and those treated with the device alone. The release did not describe the trial's design, enrollment criteria or statistical methodology beyond the two response-rate figures and patient counts. Dr. Lucía Graña-López of Spain gave a presentation titled 'Beyond Biopsy: Image-Guided Therapy in Practice,' and Dr. Francesca Pugliese of Italy presented findings specific to elderly breast cancer patients who are not candidates for surgery, according to the release. The conclusions of either presentation were not detailed in the company's statement. Two clinical workshops at the meeting, led by Dr. Graña-López and by Dr. Federica Di Naro of Italy, each attracted approximately 70 participants, IceCure said. The company separately noted research posters from Dr. Georgiana-Cristiana Camen of Romania, covering a single-center efficacy and safety study, and from Dr. Pugliese, covering contrast-enhanced mammography findings tied to the cryoablation procedure. IceCure said ProSense holds U.S. clearance for a defined patient group: women aged 70 and older with biologically low-risk tumors of 1.5 centimetres or smaller who are receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy, including patients who are not surgical candidates. The company described this as the only such clearance currently held for local breast cancer treatment in that population; that characterization rests on the company's own statement. The release gave no figures on revenue, device sales or reimbursement status tied to the EUSOBI presentations, and did not state whether any additional clinical or regulatory filings are planned as a result of the data shown. IceCure Medical is listed on Nasdaq under the ticker ICCM and is based in Caesarea, Israel.

item.title: Euro Tech forms Norway joint venture for ballast water treatment
item.description: Euro Tech Global and Sea Clean AS will jointly operate CleanPACT Environmental and Marine Engineering AS, a customer experience center for the company's PortoBallast system in Torvastad, Norway.
item.content:encoded: Euro Tech Holdings Company Limited (Nasdaq: CLWT) said on Oct. 12, 2026 that its wholly owned subsidiary, Euro Tech Global Pte Ltd, has signed a 50/50 joint venture agreement with Sea Clean AS, a Norwegian provider of ballast water treatment solutions for the maritime industry. The joint venture is named CleanPACT Environmental and Marine Engineering AS. The release does not disclose financial terms of the agreement. CleanPACT will function as what the release calls a customer experience center for port ballast water treatment, offering hands-on demonstrations, expert servicing, realistic simulations and tailored training. It is built around Euro Tech's PortoBallast system, described in the release as a next-generation mobile hybrid unit designed to treat ballast water from vessels whose existing UV or electrolysis-type treatment systems do not meet discharge compliance requirements. The release describes the venture as combining Euro Tech's technology, expertise and capabilities with Sea Clean's local knowledge, port experience and market reach. Sea Clean AS is described in the release as a Norwegian provider of ballast water treatment solutions and an authorized agent for an electrolysis-type ballast water treatment system, handling distribution, service and maintenance of such systems. The release states the company has served more than 2,300 vessels and that its technicians provide service from system installation through annual compliance checks. Euro Tech Global Pte Ltd, the Euro Tech subsidiary that is party to the joint venture, is described only as a wholly owned subsidiary of the parent company. According to the release, Sea Clean is setting up and commissioning the PortoBallast unit, which has recently arrived at Sea Clean's port site in Torvastad, Norway. The release does not state when commissioning will be complete or when the center will begin operating. Euro Tech said the new joint venture will also promote PortoBallast across Scandinavia, which the release describes as a stepping stone to entering the European market, and that the company believes this will give it a new sales platform for global promotion. The release discloses no financial terms for the joint venture — it gives no investment figures, no revenue-sharing arrangement and no governance details beyond the stated 50/50 ownership split between Euro Tech Global and Sea Clean. It also does not state a date for CleanPACT to begin full operations, nor does it mention any regulatory or corporate approvals required before the arrangement is considered complete. The release is dated Oct. 12, 2026 and carries no closing or effective date for the joint venture agreement itself beyond its having been signed. The release includes a standard forward-looking-statements disclaimer under the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, saying the company can give no assurance regarding actual outcomes and naming risk factors that include its Hong Kong and China operations, competition, dependence on vendors, product development, market entry, business downturns, personnel availability and the negotiation of agreements.

item.title: Scottie Resources closes C$21.4-million private placement
item.description: The brokered and non-brokered tranches issued 7.36 million shares, with a second non-brokered tranche of about C$2.6 million expected around October 14.
item.content:encoded: Scottie Resources Corp. (TSXV: SCOT) (OTCQB: SCTSF) (FSE: SR80) closed a brokered private placement and the initial tranche of a non-brokered private placement on October 9, 2026. The combined offering issued 7,359,870 shares, including 194,212 flow-through shares, at C$2.90 per common share and C$3.10 per flow-through share, for aggregate gross proceeds of C$21,382,465.40. The brokered tranche was conducted under an agency agreement dated October 9, 2026, with Velocity Capital Partners acting as sole bookrunner, alongside Agentis Capital Markets and Beacon Securities Limited as agents. In connection with the brokered offering, the company paid the agents a cash fee of C$442,457.99 and issued 152,572 compensation warrants, each exercisable at C$2.90 per share until October 9, 2028. For the initial tranche of the non-brokered offering, the company paid cash finder's fees of C$330,306.64 and issued 113,899 finder's warrants on the same terms as the compensation warrants. The release described the non-brokered offering as proceeding in tranches, with the first tranche closing alongside the brokered placement. Related parties purchased 1,379,310 of the non-brokered common shares and 24,565 of the flow-through shares in the offering, which the company said represented less than 25% of its market capitalization. All securities issued in the offering are subject to a statutory hold period expiring February 10, 2027. The company said net proceeds from the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, including technical studies and permitting work at the Scottie Gold Mine Project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle. Proceeds from the flow-through shares are earmarked for Canadian exploration expenses, which the company intends to renounce to subscribers effective December 31, 2026. Scottie Resources said it anticipates closing a further non-brokered tranche of approximately C$2.6 million on or about October 14, 2026, subject to the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange and other customary conditions. The company's flagship project is the Scottie Gold Mine, located in British Columbia's Golden Triangle region.

item.title: Algo8 AI secures final approval to list on CSE
item.description: Trading in the industrial AI company's shares, under the symbol AIOS, is expected to begin on or about October 13, following an October 6 plan of arrangement.
item.content:encoded: Algo8 AI Inc. received final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange to list its common shares under the symbol "AIOS" (CUSIP 016917106, ISIN CA0169171067), with trading expected to begin on or about October 13, 2026. The listing follows the October 6, 2026 closing of a previously announced plan of arrangement under which the company acquired the Algo8 business. Shares issued to former Algo8 Industrial AI Inc. shareholders and finders in connection with the arrangement, representing approximately 66.06% of the issued and outstanding shares, are subject to restrictions on transfer. Founders, management and advisors are restricted from trading for the first 12 months after listing, with shares released in stages through the 36-month anniversary of the trading date. Shares issued to Chemelex LLC and finders carry a shorter lock-up, releasing 50% six months after the trading date and the remaining 50% at 12 months. The company's PlantBrain industrial AI operating system has more than 80 deployments across the steel, tire, automotive and energy sectors, according to the release, with operations across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. The release said customer engagements have expanded from single-site installations to multi-site programs. Among those engagements, the company cited a Phase 1 multi-plant deployment with a global tire manufacturer, under an initial contract valued at approximately $4.0 million, plus the potential for recurring support revenue. The release's forward-looking statements caution that this potential recurring revenue may not be realized. The release also cited a $2.79 million strategic investment in the company from Chemelex LLC, without stating when that investment was made relative to the arrangement or the listing. The company's leadership includes Co-Founder and CEO Nandan Mishra, a graduate of IIT Kanpur and a former Google Maps engineer; Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer Himanshu Singh, also an IIT Kanpur graduate; and President and Director Brandon Kou, formerly chief executive of the publicly traded Leef Brands. Trading in Algo8 AI's shares is expected to begin on or about October 13, 2026, on the Canadian Securities Exchange under the symbol AIOS, with the listing completing the company's transition to a standalone, independent publicly traded entity following the arrangement.

item.title: StatCan releases first sector-based producer price indexes
item.description: The new quarterly measure, developed with the Bank of Canada, tracks price changes across energy, non-energy, goods and services sectors, covering the second quarter of 2026.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada released the Sector-based Producer Price Indexes for the first time on October 9, 2026, covering the second quarter of 2026. The agency said the indexes measure price changes across four broad producer sectors it names as energy, non-energy, goods and services. The methodology behind the series was developed by the Bank of Canada. Statistics Canada said the indexes are intended to support research and analysis of firms' price-setting behaviour and inflation dynamics, including the development of economic models. The agency said the indexes are published quarterly and are not seasonally adjusted, and are available only at the national level. It said the previous two quarters of data are revised with every release, and the full series is revised back to the start of the weight reference year whenever the index weights are updated. The Daily notice itself reports no specific index values or period-over-period changes for the quarter; it introduces the new series' scope and methodology. Statistics Canada listed separate telephone numbers and email addresses for inquiries about the indexes' concepts, methods and data quality, and for media inquiries.

item.title: Spectre Capital enters promissory note with Northern Rare Earth
item.description: The non-interest-bearing loan of up to C$100,000 funds Spectre's costs tied to its proposed qualifying transaction with Northern Rare Earth Corp.
item.content:encoded: Spectre Capital Corp. (TSX-V: SOO.P) said it has entered into a non-interest-bearing, unsecured grid promissory note with Northern Rare Earth Corp. ("NREC"), under which NREC will lend Spectre up to C$100,000. Spectre said the loan will be used exclusively to fund its direct, bona fide, third-party transaction expenses in connection with its proposed qualifying transaction with NREC, as previously announced in its news releases dated May 28, 2026, and August 18, 2026. The release describes Spectre as a capital pool company — a listed shell with no operating business, used under TSX Venture Exchange rules to raise a small amount of seed capital and then identify an operating business to combine with in what the exchange calls a qualifying transaction. Under that structure, Spectre is the public vehicle and NREC is the business it has proposed to combine with. The loan takes the form of a grid promissory note, meaning it can be drawn down in multiple advances up to the C$100,000 ceiling rather than disbursed as a single sum; each advance requires NREC's prior written approval, the release said. No finder's fee, commission or other compensation is payable in connection with the loan. The outstanding principal balance is payable in full once the qualifying transaction completes. Spectre said that if the transaction does not close and the definitive amalgamation agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms, the outstanding balance will instead be forgiven in full. Trading in Spectre's shares has been halted in compliance with TSX Venture Exchange policy; the release said trading will remain halted pending the exchange's review of the qualifying transaction and satisfaction of its conditions for resumption.

item.title: St-Georges files Q1 results, details steps to resume trading
item.description: The company reported a $681,444 net loss and said it will work with regulators toward lifting the failure-to-file cease trade order issued September 30.
item.content:encoded: St-Georges Eco-Mining Corp. (CSE: SX) said it has filed its unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements, related management's discussion and analysis, and required officer certifications for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The company reported a net loss of $681,444 and a net and comprehensive loss of $683,095 for the period. It said total assets were $25,725,934 and shareholders' equity was $18,801,233, with a working capital deficiency of $5,616,857. The company said its financial statements include disclosure of material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on its ability to continue as a going concern. It said management's plans depend, among other factors, on increased battery-processing activity at its EVSX subsidiary, access to financing, cost reductions and arrangements with creditors. The filings follow a failure-to-file cease trade order the British Columbia Securities Commission issued on September 30, 2026, which suspended trading in St-Georges shares on the Canadian Securities Exchange. St-Georges said that filing the outstanding documents does not, by itself, revoke the cease trade order. St-Georges said it will engage with the BCSC and the CSE to advance the steps required to seek revocation, which it described as including confirming the status of its continuous disclosure record, responding to any regulatory comments or requests for additional information, and completing any further requirements identified by the applicable authorities. The company said it cannot provide a definitive date for the revocation of the cease trade order or the resumption of trading. St-Georges describes itself in the release as a company that develops new technologies and holds a diversified portfolio of assets and patent-pending intellectual property across several subsidiaries, including EVSX, a battery-processing initiative, along with St-Georges Metallurgy, Iceland Resources, H2SX and exploration projects in Quebec.

item.title: Canadian employment fell 68,000 in September
item.description: Statistics Canada said the unemployment rate rose to 6.5% as the employment rate slipped to 60.6%.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada said employment fell by 68,000, or 0.3%, in September 2026, for the reference period of September 13 to 19. The unemployment rate rose 0.1 percentage points to 6.5%, the employment rate fell 0.2 percentage points to 60.6%, and the labour force participation rate fell 0.2 percentage points to 64.8%. The decline was split between full-time employment, down 35,000, or 0.2%, and part-time employment, down 33,000, or 0.9%, the agency said in its monthly Labour Force Survey. By industry, Statistics Canada reported declines in educational services (-35,000, or -2.2%), health care and social assistance (-23,000, or -0.8%), and manufacturing (-13,000, or -0.7%). It reported growth in other services, a category covering repair, maintenance and personal services, which rose 17,000, or 2.1%. Statistics Canada said employment among youth aged 15 to 24 fell by 48,000, or 1.8%, and among core-aged women aged 25 to 54 fell by 28,000, or 0.4%, with the unemployment rate for that group rising to 5.3%. By region, the agency reported employment declines in Quebec (-49,000, or -1.1%), British Columbia (-20,000, or -0.7%) and Manitoba (-4,400, or -0.6%), and increases in Alberta (+23,000, or +0.9%), Newfoundland and Labrador (+1,800, or +0.7%) and Prince Edward Island (+1,000, or 1.0%). Statistics Canada said average hourly wages among employees rose 2.3% year over year, up 86 cents, to $37.64. It also reported that public sector employment fell by 70,000, or 1.5%, for a fourth consecutive month, self-employment fell by 23,000, or 0.8%, the job-finding rate declined to 30.6% from 32.8% a year earlier, and the layoff rate was 0.7%, compared with 0.6% a year earlier.

item.title: Evernorth completes business combination, lists on Nasdaq
item.description: The combined company holds about 473 million XRP and roughly $300 million in gross cash proceeds, with trading set to begin October 12.
item.content:encoded: Evernorth Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) said it completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on October 9, 2026. The company describes itself as "a digital asset treasury company building institutional access to the XRP economy at scale." Evernorth said that at closing it held approximately 473 million XRP and had raised approximately $300 million in gross cash proceeds, before transaction expenses. Trading in Evernorth's shares on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN is set to begin October 12, 2026. Armada Acquisition Corp. II was a special purpose acquisition company — a listed vehicle that raises capital and then seeks to combine with an operating business. In a completed business combination of this kind, the public shell and any additional investment raised alongside the closing become the capital of the surviving company, which in this case is Evernorth. Citigroup Global Markets Inc. acted as sole private placement agent and capital markets advisor to Evernorth, with Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP serving as the company's legal counsel. Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, P.C. served as legal counsel to Armada; Cohen and Company Capital Markets and Northland Securities Inc. advised Armada, and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP advised Citigroup, according to the release. The company said its strategy is "strategies designed to grow XRP per share over time through institutional and DeFi yield strategies, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities." Chief executive Asheesh Birla said: "We'll be deploying capital across the XRP economy, supporting the infrastructure and use cases that expand XRP's utility." The release names Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR as investors in the transaction, and identifies Arrington XRP Capital Fund, LP as sponsor of the Armada vehicle. Evernorth said it expects to ring the Nasdaq closing bell on October 14, 2026, an event it said will bring together company leadership, investors and members of the XRP ecosystem. Trading under the ticker XRPN begins two days earlier, on October 12, 2026.

item.title: IT Tech Packaging wins NYSE American extension to April 2027
item.description: NYSE Regulation granted the extension after the company missed three SEC filings, including its 2025 annual report.
item.content:encoded: IT Tech Packaging, Inc. (NYSE American: ITP) said NYSE Regulation has accepted its request for an extension of time to regain compliance with the exchange's continued listing standards. The company said it submitted its extension request on October 1, 2026, and that NYSE Regulation accepted it on October 7, 2026, granting a plan period running to what the company called a "New Cure Deadline" of April 15, 2027. The company describes itself in the release as a manufacturer and distributor of diversified paper products in North China, founded in 1996 and based in Baoding, producing corrugating medium paper, offset printing paper and tissue products using recycled paper as its primary raw material, with the exception of its tissue products. IT Tech Packaging said it failed to timely file its Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, and its Form 10-Q reports for the quarters ended March 31, 2026, and June 30, 2026, putting it in violation of Sections 134 and 1101 of the NYSE American Company Guide, which require timely filing of periodic reports with the SEC. The company said its common stock will continue to be listed and trade on NYSE American during the plan period, now carrying a ".LF" indicator marking it as a late filer, subject to its compliance with the plan and other applicable continued listing requirements. IT Tech Packaging said that if it does not make progress consistent with the plan, or fails to complete the delayed filings by the April 15, 2027 deadline, NYSE Regulation staff will initiate delisting proceedings as appropriate; it said it may appeal such a determination under Section 1010 and Part 12 of the NYSE American Company Guide. The release does not state why the three filings were delayed.

item.title: Intermap completes $7.7 million buyout of PCI Geomatics
item.description: The TSX-listed geospatial software company now owns all of CATALYST developer PCI Geomatics, after a court-approved arrangement closed October 7.
item.content:encoded: Intermap Technologies Corporation (TSX: IMP) said October 7 it had completed its acquisition of PCI Geomatics Group Inc., paying $7.7 million in cash for the shares of PCI it did not already own. The transaction proceeded as an arrangement under the Canada Business Corporations Act. PCI shareholders approved the arrangement on September 25, 2026, and the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, Commercial List, issued the final order on September 28, 2026. PCI operates its software under the brand CATALYST, an imagery analytics platform the release describes as having more than 30,000 installed software licences in over 150 countries, used to process and analyze satellite and aerial imagery. Intermap said the acquisition adds PCI's optical image processing and distributed edge-processing capabilities to its own 3D data, processing and analytics offerings. The release describes the cash paid as being for the PCI shares Intermap did not already own, indicating Intermap held a stake in PCI prior to this transaction; it does not state the size of that prior holding or when it was acquired. Patrick Blott, Intermap's chairman and chief executive, said the deal lets the company push its capabilities 'closer to the edge through the software and agreements already in our customers' hands, without disruption to workflows.' June McAlarey, PCI's president and chief executive and now an Intermap executive vice president, said combining PCI's edge-processing capability with Intermap's 3D data and analytics 'gives us more ways to solve those problems and reduce latencies.' Alongside the closing, Intermap issued 2027 guidance projecting commercial revenue of $12 million to $15 million, representing growth of more than 100%, adjusted EBITDA of approximately $5 million and contribution margins above 50%, excluding government procurement revenue, which the company said carries timing uncertainty. The release does not disclose how much of that projected revenue is attributable to PCI specifically rather than Intermap's existing business. The release does not state PCI's standalone revenue or earnings prior to the acquisition, so the contribution the deal itself makes to the 2027 guidance figures above cannot be isolated from organic growth in Intermap's existing operations. The guidance is the company's own forward projection and has not yet been realized.

item.title: Nord Precious Metals closes $1.6-million flow-through placement
item.description: The non-brokered financing will fund exploration at the Castle East project in Ontario, with finder's fees of $112,000 cash and warrants.
item.content:encoded: Nord Precious Metals Mining Inc. (TSX.V: NTH) closed a non-brokered private placement of 8,888,888 flow-through shares priced at $0.18 each on October 7, 2026, for gross proceeds of $1,600,000. The announcement, issued from the company's Cobalt, Ontario office, states the financing remains subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange. The release states that proceeds will be used for exploration on the company's Castle East project, and that the spending will qualify as Canadian exploration expenses and as flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures. It gives no further detail on the exploration program itself — no target, no budget breakdown and no timeline beyond the financing's close. Finders are to be paid $112,000 in cash — 7% of the gross proceeds — and issued 622,222 non-transferable warrants, also calculated at 7%, each exercisable at $0.18 per share for two years from closing, subject to exchange approval. All securities in the placement, including the finder's warrants, are subject to a hold period of four months and one day, expiring February 8, 2027, and the financing as a whole remains conditional on final TSX Venture Exchange acceptance. The release names Frank J. Basa as chief executive officer and Wayne Cheveldayoff as the company's corporate communications contact. Nord Precious Metals, which trades as TSX.V: NTH, OTCQB: NPMMF and FSE: QN3, describes itself as focused on silver recovery and exploration in Ontario's Cobalt-Gowganda mining camp, where it also operates the TTL Laboratories processing facility; Castle East is the target of this round of spending. The release does not disclose a drilling program, a budget breakdown within the $1,600,000, or a timeline for exploration results at Castle East. It is a financing disclosure rather than a technical one, and what the money will find at the project is not addressed.

item.title: Heliostar graduates from TSX Venture Exchange to TSX
item.description: Common shares began trading on the senior exchange October 7 under the unchanged symbol HSTR, with no action required of shareholders.
item.content:encoded: Heliostar Metals Ltd.'s common shares commenced trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange at market open on October 7, 2026, following the company's graduation from the TSX Venture Exchange. The shares continue to trade under the symbol HSTR, with the same CUSIP and ISIN numbers as before. They were voluntarily delisted from the TSXV effective market close on October 6, 2026. The release states that shareholders are not required to take any action, exchange share certificates, or do anything else in connection with the change, and that the CUSIP and ISIN numbers are unchanged. Chief executive Charles Funk said: "A big-board TSX listing rewards shareholders with greater trading liquidity, potential for additional index inclusions and broader capital markets exposure to support the growth of the Company." Heliostar operates two producing mines in Mexico, La Colorada in Sonora and San Agustin in Durango, and lists three development projects: Ana Paula in Guerrero, Cerro del Gallo in Guanajuato, and Goldstrike in Utah. The company has stated a goal of reaching 500,000 ounces of annual gold production by the end of the decade. The release states the company is targeting completion of the Ana Paula feasibility study in the first half of 2027, with commercial production contemplated for 2028. Those are the company's own stated targets; the release discloses no technical or financial detail behind either date. The release does not disclose trading volumes, an index weighting, or any financial detail tied to the change — it is a notice of the venue change and the operational and development context the company gives alongside it, nothing more.

item.title: Georgia Street Capital raises $250,000 in TSX Venture IPO
item.description: The capital pool company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange October 6 and begins searching for a business to acquire via a Qualifying Transaction.
item.content:encoded: Georgia Street Capital Corp. completed its initial public offering on October 6, 2026, issuing 2,500,000 common shares at $0.10 per share for gross proceeds of $250,000, and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange the same day as a capital pool company under the symbol GOST.P. The shares were listed and immediately halted pending completion of the offering; trading is expected to commence at the market open on or about October 8, 2026. A capital pool company is a shell corporation listed under TSX Venture Exchange Policy 2.4 with no commercial operations and no assets other than cash raised in its initial offering. Georgia Street's release states the corporation intends to identify and evaluate businesses with a view to completing a Qualifying Transaction — the process by which a CPC acquires an operating business and converts from a shell into a regular listed issuer. No target or sector has been disclosed. Leede Financial Inc. acted as agent for the offering. Its compensation was a cash commission equal to 10% of gross proceeds, a corporate finance fee of $15,000, and non-transferable options to purchase up to 250,000 shares at $0.10 per share, exercisable until October 6, 2031. The release discloses no other fees paid in connection with the offering. Georgia Street now has 8,832,000 shares issued and outstanding. Of those, 6,632,000 shares held in aggregate by the corporation's directors, officers and seed shareholders are subject to escrow restrictions. The release does not state the length of the escrow or the conditions for its release. The corporation's officers and directors are Steven Vanry, who holds the roles of chief executive, chief financial officer and corporate secretary in addition to his board seat, and directors Kevin Bottomley and Craig Roberts. The release discloses no further detail on their backgrounds or on how the seed shares were allocated among them. The release does not state what Georgia Street intends to do with the $250,000 raised beyond its general purpose of pursuing a Qualifying Transaction, nor does it name any industry or target company under consideration. A reader should not infer that an acquisition is pending or imminent — none is disclosed. The capital pool company mechanism is how the TSX Venture Exchange brings new shell vehicles to market ahead of an eventual business combination, and this listing follows that structure. Whether Georgia Street attracts a Qualifying Transaction, and on what terms, is not yet determined; the release discloses no timeline and no prospective target.

item.title: Athos Metals closes first tranche as Meed Growth deal deadline extended
item.description: Athos raised $1,276,799.96 in two classes of subscription receipt, held in escrow, as the outside date for its proposed reverse take-over of Meed moves to October 31.
item.content:encoded: Meed Growth Corp. (TSXV: MEED.P), a capital pool company, announced on October 6, 2026 that Athos Metals Corp. has closed the first tranche of its non-brokered private placement for aggregate gross proceeds of $1,276,799.96. Athos issued 5,720,000 subscription receipts at $0.10 each, for $572,000, and 5,873,333 flow-through subscription receipts at $0.12 each, for $704,799.96. The release presents the placement as the concurrent financing for the proposed transaction between the two companies. That transaction would, if completed, result in the reverse take-over of Meed by Athos and constitute Meed's Qualifying Transaction under the TSX Venture Exchange's Policy 2.4 – Capital Pool Companies. On completion, Meed, referred to in the release as the Resulting Issuer, will carry on the business of Athos. Meed was incorporated in British Columbia on February 2, 2021; according to the release, it has not commenced commercial operations and has no assets other than cash and cash equivalents. The receipts make the money conditional on the transaction. The gross proceeds of the first tranche are held in escrow pending certain escrow release conditions, including the satisfaction or waiver of all conditions precedent to the transaction. Once those are met, each subscription receipt entitles its holder, without further payment or action, to one common share of Athos, and each flow-through subscription receipt to one Athos share that will qualify as a flow-through share. Upon completion of the transaction, the Athos shares issued on the receipts will be exchanged for common shares of the Resulting Issuer, and the flow-through Athos shares for flow-through common shares of the Resulting Issuer. If the escrow release conditions are not satisfied by 5:00 p.m. Vancouver time on November 30, 2026, a deadline extended from September 30, 2026, the receipts will be cancelled and holders will be entitled to their aggregate purchase price plus a pro rata share of any interest earned. The two classes of receipt are earmarked differently. Athos will incur Canadian exploration expenses qualifying as critical mineral exploration expenditures in an amount equal to the aggregate issue price of the flow-through receipts, to be renounced to subscribers with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The proceeds of the ordinary subscription receipts will be used to advance exploration on Athos' mineral properties and for working capital and general corporate purposes. Finder's compensation is payable only once the escrow release conditions are satisfied. Athos will pay $29,750.01 in cash, representing 7% of the first-tranche gross proceeds received from subscribers introduced by finders, and issue 266,000 non-transferable finder's warrants, representing 7% of the receipts issued to those subscribers. Each warrant is exercisable for one Athos share at $0.10 for 24 months from issue. Securities issued in the placement, and any finder's securities, are subject to applicable statutory hold periods and any exchange escrow or resale restrictions. Separately, Meed and Athos have entered into an extension letter to their binding merger agreement dated May 28, 2026. It moves the outside date for completing the transaction from September 30, 2026 to October 31, 2026, or such later date as the two companies agree in writing. Athos anticipates closing one or more additional tranches of the placement. For readers following capital pool company transactions, the release sets out the dates this one now depends on. The outside date of October 31 falls a month before the November 30 escrow deadline, and the outside date can be moved again by written agreement. Until the conditions are met, subscribers hold receipts rather than shares. The release cautions that there can be no assurance the transaction will be completed on the terms proposed or at all, and that trading in Meed's securities should be considered highly speculative.

item.title: Big Bear Gold to resume TSXV trading after Peerless option assignment
item.description: Shares halted since September 28 are expected to reopen on October 8, after the company agreed to acquire Bathurst Metals' 100% optioned interest in the Peerless Property.
item.content:encoded: Big Bear Gold Corp. (TSXV: BEAR) announced on October 6, 2026 that its common shares are expected to resume trading on the TSX Venture Exchange at market open on Thursday, October 8, 2026. Trading in the shares was halted on September 28, 2026, pending the announcement of the company's acquisition of an optioned interest in the Peerless Property. The announcement is a short notice, and the disclosure in it is limited. The transaction behind the halt is an assignment and assumption of property option agreement dated September 25, 2026, between the company, Bathurst Metals Corp. and Stanley R McClay, as bare trustee for BCT Holdings Corp. Under it, Big Bear will acquire Bathurst Metals' 100% optioned interest in the Peerless Property, located in the Bridge River Mining Camp in British Columbia. The transaction is subject to TSXV approval. The notice does not restate the consideration or the terms of the underlying option. It states that full details of the transaction are set out in the company's news release dated October 1, 2026. This entry draws only on the resumption notice; a reader looking for the price and the option terms should go to that earlier release, and to the exchange's decision on approval. Beyond its location in the Bridge River Mining Camp, the notice gives no information on the property itself, such as its size, mineralization or past work, and no closing date. The company describes itself as focused on acquiring and developing mineral properties with strong potential to host significant resources in Western Canada. For holders, the practical change is the date: shares halted since September 28 are expected to trade again from the open on October 8, with the transaction still subject to TSXV approval.

item.title: Elton Resources begins TSX Venture trading and grants 12.7 million options
item.description: The former Chicane Capital I Corp. opened under the symbol DBAY on October 6, engaged ICP Securities Inc. for market-making and granted options exercisable at $0.20 for 10 years.
item.content:encoded: Elton Resources Corp. (TSXV: DBAY), formerly Chicane Capital I Corp., announced that its common shares commenced trading on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol DBAY at market open on October 6, 2026. The company describes itself as a mining exploration company focused on the exploration and development of its flagship Darnley Bay Project in the Northwest Territories. The release's cautionary language refers to the company's qualifying transaction and states that trading in its securities should be considered highly speculative. Carson Phillips, the company's chief executive officer, said: “We believe Darnley Bay represents one of the most compelling geophysical anomalies in the world, and the closing of this transaction marks a historical moment for the Project.” He added that the anomaly has “attracted scientific and exploration interest for decades”, and that the company plans to advance its targets with what he called “a robust drilling program”. According to the release, Darnley Bay hosts a large gravity and magnetic anomaly that is considered one of the strongest isolated gravity anomalies in the world. It has a gravity amplitude of 132 mGal and dimensions of 80 km by 100 km, with a coincident magnetic anomaly of 1,350 nT.
